### Items, red first

1. **Red, compiling.** New `harness/tests/layout_place.rs`. Through `Viewer::run_command` and once through the process (the method of `harness/tests/layout_pdf_host.rs:292`): `document.new` profile `layout` 595 x 842 pt (`harness-core/src/document_new.rs:298-300`); `asset.place` of an embedded 64 x 48 PNG written by the test into a frame on `page-1`; `layout.export_pdf`; assert `tiles_drawn` > 0 (summary field `layout_export.rs:727`) and no `raster_unresolved` loss; `layout.render_pdf_page` of page 0 and assert pixels inside the frame are not white and pixels just outside it are white (clip). Commands are strings, so the red commit compiles. Prove red by running: today `asset.place` refuses `canvas_unavailable`.

2. **Place into a frame.** New egui-free `harness-view/src/view/layout_place.rs`; `place.rs` gains only a branch at `:681` (and `:639`) that hands a pages-only document to it.
   - `asset.place` gains optional `page`, `frame_x`, `frame_y`, `frame_width`, `frame_height` (pt, page coordinates: the record's `bounds`), `shape` (`rectangle` | `ellipse`; a `Path` frame needs a vector path id and refuses `frame_shape_unsupported` in this slice), `fit` (the `StudioFit` tokens legal for a frame: not `honour_existing_style`, fitting.rs docs), `frame_fitting`, `anchor`. On a pages-only document `page` and the four frame numbers are required (`frame_required`; see open question).
   - Pixels: the layer's tiles hold the SOURCE at its own pixel size (no resample, no canvas clip), so the PDF carries the full resolution; `content_width`/`content_height` = pixels x 72 / source ppi (open question for the ppi source). Bound `MAX_PLACE_PIXELS` (`place.rs:100`), refused before decode where the header gives the size.
   - Records: one raster layer whose parent chain reaches the page's spread (otherwise PDF reports `layer_not_on_page_spread`, `pdf_export.rs:668-671`); its `StudioRasterLayerRecord.placed_asset` and `Instance` in the `raster_records` entry as on artboards; one `StudioGraphicFrame` in `longdoc.graphic_frames`. Follow how `LayoutEdit::DrawFrame` adds a layer to the layout document (NOT_INSPECTED: its layer-graph handling; read `layout_ui.rs` `transform` DrawFrame arm before writing).
   - ONE undo step: new `Run::submit_layout_and_entry(op, command, document, records, token, bytes)` beside `submit_layout` (`harness.rs:2053`), committing the `LayoutStep` and the entry into one `HistoryStep` (both fields `layout` and `entry` exist, `harness.rs:358-380`), modelled on `restructure_and_entry_step` (`:1492-1532`): a refused entry write undoes the layout half, no split step. NOT_INSPECTED: whether the undo and redo dispatch applies both fields of one step; read it first and extend it there if not. Test: undo removes layer, frame and entry bytes together; redo restores them byte-identically.

3. **Fit.** New row `asset.fit` (name: open question) in `commands/asset.rs`, arm in `view/commands/place.rs:22`: `{layer, fit, anchor?, crop_top?, crop_left?, crop_bottom?, crop_right?, frame_fitting?}` re-fits a graphic frame through `fit_content`; `frame_to_content` resizes the frame record; `apply_frame_fitting_options` uses the stored rule and refuses without one; one layout step; a layer without a frame refuses `layer_not_graphic_frame`.

4. **Links on layout frames.** `list_placements` (`place.rs:922`) lists layout placements with `page_id`, frame bounds, fit and the derived `effective_ppi` and `actual_ppi` (STU-LAY-132 last paragraph, spec :6168 block). `update_all_modified` (`:936`) re-decodes a layout placement at source resolution, not through `placement_tiles`' canvas clip, and keeps its frame. `transform.move`, `transform.free_transform`, `transform.reset` (`place.rs:773-785`) on a graphic-frame layer refuse `graphic_frame_transform_unsupported`: moving the pixels while the frame record stays would draw wrong; frame move is a later slice.

5. **The layout PDF draws it.** `layout_export.rs`, hunks `:52-57` (docs), `:193-205`, `:665-698` only; never `:740-776` (SMB-TYPE-INDENT-SPACING-1 edits `:768-775`).
   - `NoAssets` replaced by a resolver in new `view/layout_assets.rs`: `raster(layer_id)` builds `PlacedRaster` from the layer's `TileRef`s and their bodies (the `ResolvedTile` shape as `view/brush_mix.rs:75-76` `tile_view` builds it; NOT_INSPECTED: where a reopened package's tile bodies are read from, read how `render` gets them before writing); `profile(id)` gives the working profile's bytes; `path` stays `None` (rectangle and ellipse only).
   - `PdfLongDoc.graphics` filled from `place_graphic` for every record in `rec.longdoc.graphic_frames`.
   - STU-ASSET-009 gate before any shaping: a linked layout placement whose state is `missing`, `unauthorized` or `unsupported` refuses `placed_link_missing`, `placed_link_unauthorized`, `placed_link_unsupported` (codes of `place.rs:53-65`) and writes nothing; `modified` refuses `placed_link_modified` (open question). The summary gains `placements`: per placement `layer_id`, `source_id`, `placement_kind`, `uri`, content digest and link state at resolution time.
   - Module docs `:52-57`: placed graphics drawn; vector paths, tables, outlines, CMYK image numbers stay declared gaps.

6. **Docs and MTs.** `place.rs` module manual (`:1-75`) gains the layout section and the new codes; `commands/asset.rs` row docs. Read MT-30721, MT-30722, MT-30723, MT-30730..MT-30736, MT-157, MT-162, MT-163, MT-170 (print G5 list, NOT_INSPECTED in this plan) and claim a row only if it is read and proven here. Do not edit MT files.

Hostile input (V4-01/02), each a typed refusal that changes nothing (package bytes identical): frame numbers non-finite, zero, negative size, a side over 14400 pt (`PAGE_SIDE_PT`, `layout_export.rs:91`); unknown page; source over `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`; pixels over `MAX_PLACE_PIXELS`; the 65537th frame (`MAX_GRAPHIC_FRAMES`); a crop that empties the content box; `fit` on a layer without a frame; `content_aware`; a link outside the document folder (`link_outside_document_folder`); a canceled token during decode and during export.

Determinism: two exports of the same document are byte-identical (press export is deterministic, `press-write/src/export.rs:15-16`); save, reopen, export gives the same sha256.

Vendor parity stays UNVERIFIED (D5): 100 % at source ppi, frame-required placement and the modified-link refusal are Studio readings.

2. **Document set and link graph.** New module `harness-core/src/web_site.rs`, declared from `web_commands.rs` (`mod web_site;`) so `harness.rs` is untouched. Walk `local_root` in sorted order (never enumeration order, STU-WEB-131), bounded by file count (reuse `MAX_EXPORT_FILES` `:75`), depth (`MAX_SEGMENTS` `:81`) and the existing portable-name and no-escape rules; every `.html`/`.htm` is parsed under `Limits`; the open document contributes its live source, not its file. Per document, `collect_assets` through a recording port that keeps each reference's `Loads`. Graph row: `{from, reference, span, line, load, target_id, outcome}`; line = 1 + newlines before `span.start`. A fragment `page.html#id` to a site document resolves against that document's `id` attributes (the `#id` key form exists, `web_commands.rs:984`).

3. **`web.site_report`** (new row, `web_command`; a read, no history step, one op record with counts). Rows sorted by (document, line, reference): `broken_links` severity `warning` with referring document, target and line (STU-WEB-163); `orphaned_files` severity `info` (STU-WEB-164; the site sidecar, manifest, receipt and lock file excluded; the recipe's entry document is never an orphan); `external_links` (STU-WEB-118); `missing_alt` (`img` without `alt`) and `untitled_documents` (no `title` or an empty one) from STU-WEB-121. Declared not done: redundant nested tags, removable empty tags, lint threshold, checked-out files. Bounded by `MAX_ROWS` (`:71`) with a `truncated` count.

4. **Export of the document set** (STU-WEB-120 "which document set"). `web.export_recipe` gains `documents`: `open` (default; today's output byte-identical except item 4's page-link rule) or `site`. With `site`: every document of the set is exported from its source (minified per recipe); a link to a document of the set is that document, not an asset; assets are the union; the manifest lists every document with role `document`. In both modes a page link (`Load::Document`) with no target becomes a `link_broken` warning row in the manifest and the result instead of a refusal (STU-WEB-163); any other missing local reference still refuses `asset_missing` before anything is written (STU-ASSET-009 fail closed). `web.publish` (`:627`) publishes what the manifest lists, so it follows unchanged (read `:627-690` to confirm).

Under the site lock (item 6): refuse while the open document has unsaved edits (`document_unsaved`); compute every referring document's new source by span edits of the references (attribute values through `escape_attr`; CSS `url()` spans as text edits), honouring `site_relative_link_base` (`document` relative or `site_root` absolute), and re-base the moved document's own relative references; re-parse every result before the first write; then write each through the existing atomic writer (`:909`) and rename last; on a failed write, restore already-written files from the in-memory originals and say so in the receipt. Receipt: the move plus `{document, before, after}` byte ranges per changed reference. Not a `web.undo` step: the open document, if rewritten, is reopened from disk with a fresh history (open question). Refusals: `to` outside the root, an existing `to` (case-folded, as export's collision check `:576-591`), a sidecar, manifest, receipt or lock file.

6. **Site lock** (STU-WEB-131). `web.site_report`, export with `documents: site`, `web.move_file` and `web.publish` create `<local_root>/.studio-site.lock` exclusively with `{actor, client_session, command_id}`; contention refuses `site_locked` naming the holder, never blocks; released on every exit path (a guard). Ranking rule used: professional-workflow reach first, then engine and command depth GUI panels need, filtered by the hard rule that a lane proposed to start now shares no file hunk with an in-flight lane. Lanes 3 and 4 have reach equal to or above lane 2, but each shares files with an in-flight lane, so they carry a start gate and only one paragraph.

The in-flight lane SMB-TYPE-INDENT-SPACING-1 edits more files than the planners' list states (READ: git diff 0a733db8...lane/smb-type-indent-spacing-1, 26 files): also harness-core commands/layout.rs:30, harness-view view/commands/layout.rs:41 and :87, layout_ui.rs (imports and the ReplaceText arm :1131), layout_ui/find.rs, layout_ui/styles.rs, interop-layout folio_export.rs, data_merge.rs, lib.rs and layout xref.rs, find_change.rs. Its textflow commit 74c0f61b ('text inserted at byte 0 of a non-empty story joins the first paragraph') is the same class as the empty-story and replace_text-newline candidates.

The empty-story and layout.replace_text-newline candidates (ledger 2026-11-07T17:33:46Z and 12:31:03Z; test known_defect_replace_text_newline_keeps_one_paragraph at harness/tests/harness_drive_typed.rs:460; host loss paragraph_break_inside_paragraph_set_as_line_break at layout_export.rs:714-716) are folded into lane 3 as its first item: they live in layout textflow.rs and layout_ui.rs, both in the indent lane's files, and they decide paragraph boundaries that per-paragraph attributes rely on.

Lane 3 paragraph, SMB-TYPE-CHARACTER-ATTRIBUTES-1 (start after SMB-TYPE-INDENT-SPACING-1 merges): first, a newline in layout.replace_text ends a paragraph and an empty story stores no paragraph, removing the host loss at layout_export.rs:714-716 and the pinned defect test. Then the character record of the indent lane's next_slices (scope-20261107-text-attributes.json): per-range size, tracking, kerning, baseline shift, case and position, and an OpenType feature tag map on the story range, passed into every Type request where today features and axes are empty (layout_export.rs:305-306) and script and language are fixed to Latn and en (:302-303), with script itemization so a non-Latin paragraph shapes with its own script; edit_style and a local override command carry them; IDML import maps them. It reaches print steps 27, 39 and 43 and the quality of every exported page, and it is the record the Character, Paragraph and OpenType panels will bind to across layout, vector and raster text. Tabs, lists, drop caps, keep options and ruby follow as their own slices on top of it.

Lane 4 paragraph, SMB-BOARD-1 (start after SMB-AI-LIVE-EFFECTS-1 merges): board mode does not exist (commands/board.rs:5 is an empty list; document_new.rs:68 refuses the board profile). A first slice makes the board a page-kind container (STU-WB-120, spec line 22334) and adds sticky, shape_with_text, section and connector as StudioLayer kinds (STU-WB-102..108 and 115, spec lines 22281-22315) whose text is an ordinary text sublayer (STU-WB-104), drawn by lowering to the existing vector and text paths, with node-factory, read and mutate commands for each kind (STU-WB-134, spec line 22375), STRAIGHT and ELBOWED connectors attached to nodes and magnets that reroute on move and break visibly on delete, the validation codes of STU-WB-135, and PNG export of one board. It turns about 10 of the 27 workshop steps typed and opens a whole missing product mode, but it touches folio lib.rs (Payload) and composite, which the in-flight live-effects lane edits, and the spec ranks whiteboarding below layout and web (STU-WB-101, spec line 22275).
